Turn the map into a ranking of shapes

Source: R/add_rank_morph.R
add_rank_morph.Rd

Adds a button that lifts every polygon of a layer out of the map and lines them up in a grid, sorted by a column, all at the same size and with their rank, name and value below. Another click sends them back to their place. Shapes keep their form and colour, so readers see at a glance both where each one is and how it ranks.

Usage

add_rank_morph(
  map,
  layer_id,
  column,
  name_column,
  order = c("desc", "asc"),
  title = NULL,
  duration = 1.6,
  locale = "en-US",
  digits = 1,
  prefix = "",
  suffix = "",
  position = "top-right",
  labels = context_labels()
)

Arguments

map

A map created with mapgl::maplibre() or mapgl::mapboxgl().

layer_id

ID of a fill layer whose source is an sf object or inline GeoJSON.

column

Numeric column to sort by.

name_column

Column with the name shown under each shape.

order

"desc" (the default) puts the highest value first, "asc" the lowest.

title

Optional title shown above the grid while it is visible.

duration

Length of the animation, in seconds.

locale, digits, prefix, suffix

Number formatting for the values, as in add_view_summary().

position

Corner for the button: one of "top-right" (the default), "top-left", "bottom-right" or "bottom-left".

labels

Button texts, as returned by context_labels() (morph_sort and morph_back).

Value

The modified map object.

Details

While the shapes are out of the map, panning and zooming are paused, and the grid scrolls with the mouse wheel or a finger when it is taller than the map. On a globe the map turns flat during the animation and back to a globe at the end. Features without a value in column are left out of the grid. For small islands far from the main part of a feature (more than about twice its size away), the grid shows the main part only.

The animation is meant for a few shapes, such as the provinces of a country: it works best with up to 30 features, gives a warning from 31 to 50, and an error above 50, where shapes become too small to recognise. Readers who prefer reduced motion (an operating system setting) see the result without the animation.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
library(mapgl)

maplibre(center = c(137, 37), zoom = 4.2) |>
  add_fill_layer(
    id = "prefectures",
    source = jp_prefectures,
    fill_color = interpolate(
      column = "change",
      values = c(-7, 0, 1),
      stops = c("#b2182b", "#f7f7f7", "#2166ac")
    )
  ) |>
  add_rank_morph(
    layer_id = "prefectures",
    column = "change",
    name_column = "prefecture",
    suffix = " %",
    title = "Population change, 2020-2024"
  )
} # }
